frase_gancho.texto: The hall where the Sun, war, and earth take shape in stone.

introduccion_narrativa.texto: This is one of the largest halls in the museum, in the center of the ground floor. Here you will find the story of the Mexica, who founded México-Tenochtitlan on an islet in Lake Texcoco. In time they formed an alliance with Texcoco and Tlacopan, and the three cities collected tribute from the Gulf of Mexico to the Pacific. For the Mexica, the Sun needed blood and hearts to continue on its path. That belief shaped war, sacrifice, and art. Here are the Sun Stone, the Coatlicue, the head of Coyolxauhqui, and the Teocalli of the Sacred War. You will also see a scale model of the Tlatelolco market. Each one says something different about how they understood the world.
